title: Policy
lede: Instruments that govern how a court runs, rather than how a case is decided. An Act says what the law is and a judgment says what it means; a policy says how the institution will behave, and it binds the people who build and run the court's systems as much as the people who use them.

A policy is not legislation, so it is not kept as Akoma Ntoso: it is the document itself, transcribed, with its own numbering intact and its source PDF alongside. Where a policy carries operational obligations, they are pulled out clause by clause under Standards adherence.
note: The manifest for the policy area. A policy is not an Act and not a judgment, so it is not Akoma Ntoso: it is kept as markdown under policy/md/ with its source PDF one folder over in policy/sources/, the same pairing the rest of the corpus uses. The Policy page is generic over this list - to add a document, drop its markdown and its PDF in and add an entry here. `unit` is how that document numbers itself, so a citation reads in the document's own language rather than in ours.

documents.title: Regulations for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Courts, 2026
documents.made_by: Artificial Intelligence Committee, Supreme Court of India
documents.status_note: Published for comment on 3 June 2026, comments invited until 20 June 2026. Not in force: regulation 1(2) commences it only on a notification by the Chief Justice of India for the Supreme Court, and by the Chief Justice of each High Court for the courts under it.
documents.summary: Fifty-seven regulations, in ten chapters, on how a court may and may not use artificial intelligence. It applies to every adjudicatory and administrative function of the Supreme Court, the High Courts and every court, tribunal and statutory commission that adjudicates. It fixes the principles (human primacy, explainability, accountability, data protection), lists what AI may be used for and what it may never be used for, builds the institutions that approve and police it, and lays down the registers, audits, incident reports and disclosures a court and its vendors have to produce.
documents.why_it_matters: It is the first instrument that speaks directly to a system like DRISTI. Everything else in this corpus tells a build what the law of the case requires; this tells it what the court will require of the build itself.
